title: Introduce compact RAG tool-simulator and telemetry probe playground
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Developers building RAG pipelines and agent tool-calling workflows often need a lightweight way to iterate locally without spinning up external tool services (search, TTS, function mocks) or hooking in production telemetry. This PR adds a compact, single-file tool-simulator and a small telemetry probe that emits realistic, structured traces/metrics into the local Redwood Console dev mode. The goal is to make hands-on examples faster to run in workshops and CI, reduce onboarding friction, and provide stable inputs for quickstart-driven evals.

What this PR introduces (high level):
- compact-tool-sim/: a tiny HTTP-based tool simulator (Node + single-file Python starter) that exposes three test endpoints: /search, /summarize, /math. Each endpoint simulates latency profiles and deterministic output so prompts and evals are reproducible.
- telemetry-probe/: a minimal probe that can be run alongside the simulator; it emits span traces, token-level metrics, and custom events to the local dev console or stdout in a Redwood Console-friendly JSON envelope.
- examples/rag-playground/README.md: a guided quickstart that wires the Redwood SDK (TS + Python snippets) to the simulator and probe; includes prompts, a small test corpus, and a smoke-test harness.
- devcontainer and makefile targets to let contributors run the full playground with one command.

Files changed: compact-tool-sim/node/server.js, compact-tool-sim/python/sim.py, telemetry-probe/probe.js, examples/rag-playground/README.md, examples/rag-playground/devcontainer.json, examples/rag-playground/Makefile, examples/rag-playground/sample-index.jsonl, docs/quickstarts/rag-playground-compact.md, CI/workflows/rag-playground-smoke.yml.

Design notes and tradeoffs: The simulator intentionally keeps behavior deterministic (seeded RNG) to make automated scenario assertions reliable. Latency shaping is configurable with environment variables so tests can simulate cold/warm cache characteristics without complex infra. The telemetry probe emits compact envelopes (no PII) and provides an opt-in mode to forward to an HTTP endpoint matching Redwood Console local ingestion for easy demoing. We avoided introducing new third-party deps except small, well-maintained test helpers to keep the example lightweight.

Testing and validation: Unit-level tests included for simulator response shapes and the smoke harness. Manual validation steps are in the README and CI is wired to run the smoke workflow which spins the simulator, runs the quickstart script, and asserts a handful of output invariants (tool outputs present, telemetry envelopes emitted, and SDK call counts).

How to use locally (summary):
1) git clone && cd examples/rag-playground && make dev
2) Open the dev console (http://localhost:3000) or review stdout to confirm probe envelopes
3) Run the sample notebook or the TS/py quickstart; sample prompts are under sample-index.jsonl

Checklist: 
- [x] Example code (TS + Py)
- [x] README quickstart and smoke CI
- [x] Devcontainer and make targets
- [x] Minimal telemetry probe with local console compatibility
- [x] Deterministic simulator outputs for reliable tests

Related work: This is complementary to the heavier RAG harness in examples/rag-testbench. It is intended as a minimal onboarding path for workshops and dev playgrounds (linked Linear ENG-4729). The docs page references the longer testbench for users who need richer data and multi-tool orchestration.

Release notes: added a compact RAG playground for local development and telemetry-enabled simulator for quicker iterations and demos.

Migration notes: No runtime changes to Redwood backends. This is examples-only and opt-in by contributors.
